mainTopic: Lung problems in an animal (טריפות): a lung stuck to the chest wall, holes sealed by the wall, and cysts on the lung
overview: The amud finishes a list of animal conditions. An animal whose womb was removed is kosher. A wormy liver was permitted by the court in יבנה on the third visit of the people of עסיא. The גמרא then turns to a lung stuck to the chest wall. רב נחמן worries only if growths appear, while אבימי worries in both cases. רבא explains how to check such a lung with a thin knife. There are two traditions about רב נחמיה's lukewarm-water check, and רב אשי objects to applying it to two lobes stuck together. רב נחמן's rule that the chest wall can seal a hole in the lung is defended three times: by limiting it to the lung's natural place, by rejecting a proof from a ברייתא, and by explaining why the משנה never lists a pierced chest wall. Finally, שמואל permits a lung with cysts, but רבי ירמיה is strict like רבי יוחנן, and רבא begins a market story about רב נחמן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An animal whose womb was removed is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The list of cases continues: if the womb was taken out, the animal is still כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its womb was removed, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a list of animal conditions that started on the previous page. This line rules that losing the womb does not make the animal a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the womb is not one of the injuries that make an animal unable to live. So the animal stays כשרה and may be eaten after proper שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after שחיטה

phrases.english: If its womb was removed, it is kosher.
phrases.notes: This line continues a list that started on the previous page. 'Its' means the animal's.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְפּוּחִית שֶׁלָּהּ – כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of rulings from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removal of the womb does not make the animal a טריפה.

steps.title: The wormy liver and the three trips to Yavne
steps.stepSummary: A liver infested with worms was a real case. The people of עסיא came to יבנה three times, and on the third trip it was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its liver became infested with worms: this was an actual incident. The people of Asia went up to Yavne about it on three festivals, and on the third festival they permitted it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves to a liver full of worms. Instead of just stating the rule, it tells the story of how the rule was decided: the court in יבנה ruled it permitted only on the third visit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case was hard enough that the חכמים did not answer right away. The final ruling was that worms in the liver do not make the animal a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the great court sat after the Temple was destroyed

phrases.english: If its liver became infested with worms:
this was an actual incident,
and the people of Asia went up about it
on three festivals to Yavne,
on the third festival they permitted it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְלִיעַ כָּבֵד שֶׁלָּהּ – זֶה הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wormy liver does not make the animal a טריפה. It was permitted after a long deliberation.
steps.whatToRemember: A liver infested with worms is permitted. The court in יבנה decided this only on the third visit.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a lung stuck to the chest wall
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that if a lung is stuck to the chest wall, we do not worry. If growths appeared on it, we do worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: a lung that is stuck to the chest wall, we are not concerned about it. If it sprouted growths, we are concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: a lung found attached to the ribs. רב נחמן says this alone is not a problem, but growths on the lung are a warning sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An attachment could come from a wound in the wall, which is harmless, or from a hole in the lung, which makes the animal a טריפה. Without other signs we assume the wall caused it. Growths on the lung point to a problem in the lung itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we treat it as a possible problem

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
a lung that is attached to the chest wall,
we are not concerned about it;
phrases.notes: He means we don't worry that the lung itself has a hole.

phrases.english: if it sprouted growths, we are concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung stuck to the wall is not a concern unless growths appear on it.

steps.title: אבימי: worry in both cases
steps.stepSummary: מר יהודה in the name of אבימי disagrees: we worry whether or not there are growths.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר יהודה said in the name of אבימי: in both this case and that case, we are concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with רב נחמן. According to אבימי, any lung stuck to the wall raises a concern, even with no growths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed the wall caused the attachment unless there was a sign against that. אבימי does not make that assumption, so the possibility of a hole in the lung must always be dealt with.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, both cases alike

phrases.english: Mar Yehuda said in the name of Avimi:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה – חוֹשְׁשִׁין לָהּ.
phrases.english: both this and that, we are concerned about it.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means with growths and without growths.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דַּאֲבִימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any lung attached to the wall raises a concern, whether or not there are growths.

steps.title: How do we check it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we actually check a lung that is stuck to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking for the practical method. If there is a concern, how do we find out whether the problem is in the wall or in the lung?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'we are concerned' is not enough. We need a test that tells us where the injury really is.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we act, what is the procedure

phrases.english: How do we do it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical procedure behind the concern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method for checking whether the attachment comes from the wall or the lung.

steps.title: רבא's method: separate with a thin knife
steps.stepSummary: We separate the lung from the wall with a thin knife. A defect in the wall means the wall caused it. If there is none, the lung caused it and the animal is a טריפה, even if no air leaks out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבין בר שבא explained it to me. We bring a knife with a thin edge and separate the lung from the wall. If there is a defect in the wall, we blame the wall. If not, it comes from the lung, and the animal is a טריפה, even though the lung does not let out air.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the method. Cut the lung away from the wall carefully and see whether the wall has a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A defect found in the wall explains the attachment, so the lung is fine. If the wall is clean, we assume the lung had a hole. Even if blowing air into the lung shows no leak, it is still a טריפה, because the hole is assumed to be covered over.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that 'no air comes out' proves the lung is fine. Here the animal is a טריפה even though no air leaks.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: רָבִין בַּר שְׁבָא אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי,
phrases.english: Rava said: Ravin bar Sheva explained it to me:
we bring a knife whose edge is thin
phrases.notes: Literally 'whose mouth is weak', meaning a fine, thin blade.

phrases.english: and we separate it;
phrases.notes: We separate the lung from the chest wall.

phrases.english: if there is a defect in the wall,
we attribute it to the wall;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – מֵחֲמַת רֵיאָה הִיא, וּטְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: and if not, it is because of the lung, and it is a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קָא מַפְּקָא זִיקָא.
phrases.english: even though it does not let out air.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רָבִין בַּר שְׁבָא אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Separate the lung with a thin knife. A defect in the wall means it is kosher. No defect in the wall means a טריפה, even with no air leak.
steps.whatToRemember: With a lung stuck to the wall, the question is: is the wall damaged? If yes, it is kosher. If no, it is a טריפה.

steps.title: רב נחמיה checked in lukewarm water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף used to check such a lung in lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף would check it in lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what one sage did in practice. He checked the lung by putting it in lukewarm water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the lung in lukewarm water and inflating it shows whether bubbles come out. This seems to offer a way to declare it kosher. The next step argues about which case this story belongs to.

phrases.english: Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef
would check it in lukewarm water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בָּדֵיק לַהּ בְּפָשׁוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical check, attached here to the lung stuck to the wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung can be checked in lukewarm water.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: we attach this story to a different case
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא tells רבינא: you teach רב נחמיה's practice on the lung-and-wall case, but we teach it on רבא's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב הונא son of רב פפי said to רבינא: this story of רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף, you teach it on this case, but we teach it on רבא's case.
steps.whatsHappening: A different tradition about where the story belongs. The גמרא is setting up the next step, which quotes רבא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story about lukewarm water is not being doubted. The question is which case it goes with. Moving it to another case changes which situation it teaches about.

keyTerms.meaning: You teach (you attach the teaching to)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Huna
son of Rav Pappi said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: this story of Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef,
you teach it on this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the lung stuck to the chest wall.

phrases.english: we teach it on Rava's case,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן אַהָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן אַדְּרָבָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves step 7's story to a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In another tradition, רב נחמיה's lukewarm-water check belongs with רבא's case.

steps.title: רבא: two lobes stuck together cannot be checked
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that two lobes of the lung stuck to each other have no check that can make them kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: these two lobes of the lung that are stuck to each other have no way of being checked to make them kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule of רבא that מר זוטרא was referring to. This is the case his group attaches the story to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two lobes stick together, there is no wall to blame, so the knife test from step 6 does not help. רבא says no check can declare such a lung kosher.

phrases.english: as Rava said:
these two lobes of the lung
that are stuck to one another
have no checking to make them kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי אוּנֵּי דְּרֵיאָה דִּסְרִיכָן לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the case that step 8 mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two lung lobes stuck together cannot be checked and declared kosher.

steps.title: Even so, רב נחמיה checked in lukewarm water
steps.stepSummary: The story is repeated in its new place: on רבא's case, רב נחמיה still checked in lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף would check it in lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the story on purpose, this time attached to רבא's rule about lobes stuck together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב נחמיה disagrees with רבא's 'no check' rule. He holds that lukewarm water can test lobes stuck together, and if no bubbles appear, the lung is kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two traditions about רב נחמיה's lukewarm-water check. One attaches it to a lung stuck to the chest wall. The other attaches it to two lobes stuck together, where it goes against רבא's view that no check helps.

phrases.english: Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef
would check it in lukewarm water.
phrases.notes: Here 'it' means two lobes stuck together, which רבא said cannot be checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בָּדֵיק לַהּ בְּפָשׁוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates step 7's story in its new location, against רבא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רב נחמיה checked lobes stuck together in lukewarm water, which goes against רבא.

steps.title: רב אשי: two stuck lobes cannot be blamed on anything else
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to checking two stuck lobes in water. With the wall, we can blame the wall. With two lobes, whichever one has the hole makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: What is this? It makes sense here, with the lung and the wall, because we blame the wall and the animal is kosher. But there, with two lobes, if this one has a hole it is a טריפה, and if that one has a hole it is a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the version that applies רב נחמיה's water check to רבא's case of two lobes stuck together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lung-and-wall case there are two possible causes, so a check can show the wall caused it. With two lobes, both possible causes are the lung itself. Either way it is a hole in the lung, so no check can help.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
It makes sense / granted (sets up a contrast)
We attribute it to; we blame it on

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is attacking the water check in general. He only says it makes no sense for two lobes stuck together, because there is nothing outside the lung to blame.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי מַאי?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this: What is this?
Granted here, we blame it on the wall, and it is kosher,
phrases.notes: "Here" means a lung stuck to the chest wall, from Step 6.

phrases.english: but there —
phrases.notes: "There" means רבא's case of two lobes stuck to each other (Step 9).

phrases.english: if this one has a hole, it is a tereifa,
and if that one has a hole, it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version in Step 10 that puts רב נחמיה's water check on רבא's case
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the lukewarm-water check to two lobes stuck together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A check helps only when something outside the lung could be the cause. With two lobes, every option is a hole in the lung, so the animal is a טריפה either way.

steps.title: Did רב נחמן really say that? He said the wall can seal a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a contradiction. רב נחמן worried about a hole in the lung near the wall, yet he also said a hole sealed by the wall is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב נחמן really say this? But רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: a lung that got a hole, and the wall seals it, is kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two statements of רב נחמן against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One statement treats a possible hole in the lung by the wall as a real concern for טריפה. The other says that if the wall closes such a hole, the animal is kosher. These seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say this? (opens a contradiction)
A lung that got a hole

phrases.english: And did Rav Nachman say this?
phrases.notes: "This" means רב נחמן's ruling in step 3: if growths appear on a lung stuck to the wall, we worry it has a hole.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
A lung that got a hole, and the wall seals it, is kosher!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב אשי's objection to a contradiction between two rulings of רב נחמן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's concern about a hole in the lung at the wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wall can seal a hole and keep the animal kosher, there should be no worry about a hole where the lung touches the wall.

steps.title: It depends on whether the lung touches the wall in its natural place
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The kosher ruling is where the lung naturally lies against the wall. The concern applies in a spot that is not its natural place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. There, it is in the place where it grows. Here, it is not in the place where it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the two rulings into two different spots on the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the lung naturally rests against the wall, the wall's seal holds and the animal is kosher. Somewhere else, the seal does not count, so the hole makes it a טריפה. Both rulings stand, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
The place where the lung naturally grows against the wall

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key line in the laws of the lung. Where the hole is matters just as much as whether there is one.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
there, it is in the place where it grows,
phrases.notes: "There" is the ruling that the wall's seal makes it kosher.

phrases.english: here, it is not in the place where it grows.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָתָם בִּמְקוֹם רְבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's two rulings about a hole sealed by the wall seem to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seal in the lung's natural place against the wall makes it kosher. Anywhere else, the hole makes it a טריפה.

steps.title: Where is the lung's natural place against the wall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where exactly מקום רביתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is the place where it grows?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the answer depends on מקום רביתא, the גמרא asks for its exact location. This sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 13 is useless unless we know which spot counts. So the גמרא pins down the term.

phrases.english: And where is the place where it grows?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא מְקוֹם רְבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in Step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact location of מקום רביתא

steps.title: It is where the lobes are cut apart
steps.stepSummary: מקום רביתא is the area where the lung divides into lobes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The cuts between the lobes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the location: the area where the lung splits into separate lobes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the part of the lung that naturally lies right against the chest wall. A seal there counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The cuts between the lobes; where the lung divides into lobes

phrases.english: The cuts between the lobes.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיתּוּכֵי דְּאוּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקום רביתא is the area of the divisions between the lobes

steps.title: Back to רב נחמן's rule itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רב נחמן's statement on its own so it can discuss it: a hole sealed by the wall is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: a lung that got a hole, and the wall seals it, is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא returns to the statement it just quoted. It is setting up a discussion of that statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the statement was only used to raise a contradiction. Now the גמרא repeats it as the main topic, so it can add a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (return to a statement quoted earlier)

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
A lung that got a hole, and the wall seals it, is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the statement from Step 12, now as its own topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the lung sealed by the chest wall is kosher

steps.title: רבינא: only when the lung is tangled in the flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבינא limits רב נחמן's rule. It applies only when the lung is tangled into the flesh of the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And this is only when it is tangled in the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a condition to רב נחמן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just touching the wall is not enough for him. The lung must be wound into the flesh between the ribs for the seal to count.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when... (adds a condition)

phrases.english: Ravina said:
And this is only when it is tangled in the flesh.
phrases.notes: He means the lung is wound into the flesh of the chest wall, between the ribs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: וְהוּא דִּסְבִיךְ בְּבִשְׂרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the rule restated in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall's seal makes the lung kosher only when the lung is tangled in the flesh

steps.title: רב יוסף: then even when tangled it should be a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רבינא: if an untangled lung is a טריפה, that shows there really is a hole. Then even a tangled one should be a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to רבינא: And if it is not tangled, what? It is a טריפה. So we are saying it really has a hole. If so, even when it is tangled, it should be a טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבינא's condition by spelling out what follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the untangled lung a טריפה admits the lung truly has a hole. A real hole is a real hole, so being tangled should not save it. רב יוסף backs this up with a ברייתא in the next step, and Step 20 rejects that proof.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (pushes the idea to its result)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not ruling that a tangled lung is a טריפה. He is showing that רבינא's logic seems to lead there, as a challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to Ravina:
And if it is not tangled, what?
A tereifa.
This shows we say it has a hole.
If so, when it is tangled too!
phrases.notes: Finish the thought: it should be a טריפה as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרָבִינָא: וְאִי לָא סְבִיךְ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's condition from Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's condition that the lung must be tangled in the flesh
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an untangled lung is a טריפה, we are treating the lung as truly holed. A real hole should make it a טריפה even when tangled, which empties out רב נחמן's kosher ruling.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that only one kind of seal makes something fit again
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף backs up his challenge with a ברייתא. A man whose organ was pierced is פסול, and if it sealed up he is כשר again. The ברייתא says 'this is' a פסול that becomes fit again, and that suggests other sealed holes do not work, such as a lung sealed by the chest wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: if it was pierced, he is unfit, because the fluid leaks out. If it sealed up, he is fit, because he can have children. 'And this is' a case of something unfit that goes back to being fit. What does 'this is' come to leave out? Isn't it meant to leave out a case like ours?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to support his challenge against רבינא and רב נחמן. He reads the words 'this is' as saying that only this case gets fixed by sealing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a man's organ. A hole makes him פסול, and once it closes up he becomes כשר again. The words 'this is' sound like they limit the rule to this case alone. רב יוסף argues that this leaves out other cases, like a lung sealed by the chest wall, which should stay a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Drips or leaks out weakly, so he cannot have children
Something unfit that goes back to being fit

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about animals at all. It is about a man's body. רב יוסף uses it only for its wording, 'this is,' to learn what kinds of sealing count.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: if it was pierced, he is unfit,
phrases.notes: 'It' means a man's organ. The ברייתא is about whether such a man may marry a Jewish woman of fit lineage.

phrases.english: because it leaks out weakly;
if it sealed up, he is fit, because he can have children,
and this is a case of something unfit that returns to being fit.
'And this is' comes to exclude what?
phrases.notes: Now רב יוסף is speaking again, reading the ברייתא's wording closely.

phrases.english: Isn't it to exclude a case like this one?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is our case: a hole in the lung sealed by the chest wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source to support רב יוסף's challenge in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That a lung hole sealed by the chest wall stays a טריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a pierced organ that sealed. Its words 'this is' seem to limit 'fit again' to that case only.

steps.title: The word 'this' excludes a weak skin over a lung wound
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. 'This is' does not exclude a lung sealed by the chest wall. It excludes a thin skin that grew because of a wound in the lung, which is not a real covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude a thin skin that grew on the lung because of a wound, since that is not a real skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's proof. It says the word 'this' is leaving out a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thin skin that forms over a wound in the lung is weak and does not last, so it does not count as a seal. The chest wall is solid flesh and a lasting seal. So the ברייתא's limit does not touch רב נחמן's rule.

phrases.english: No, it comes to exclude a thin skin
that grew because of a wound in the lung,
since it is not a real skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְמַעוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of 'this is.' The ברייתא itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'this is' excludes the chest-wall case, but it can be explained as excluding a weak wound-skin instead.
steps.whatToRemember: A lung sealed by the chest wall can stay kosher, because the chest wall is a real, lasting seal. A thin skin that grows over a wound is not.

steps.title: Then the משנה should list a hole in the chest wall
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא objects to רב נחמן. If a hole in the chest wall right over the lung hole would make the animal a טריפה, then the chest wall decides the animal's status. So the משנה should have listed 'a pierced chest wall' as its own טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא challenged this: if the chest wall were pierced right opposite it, what would the law be? A טריפה! So let the משנה teach 'a pierced chest wall' as a טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב נחמן's rule. It comes from the fact that the משנה's list of טריפות does not mention the chest wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב נחמן's rule, a hole in the chest wall right where it seals the lung would undo the seal and make the animal a טריפה. That would make a hole in the chest wall its own kind of טריפה. Since the משנה does not list it, רב עוקבא suggests that the chest wall's seal should not count at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect that makes it forbidden to eat
Let it teach, meaning the משנה should have said so

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama objected to it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב נחמן's rule that a lung hole sealed by the chest wall is kosher.

phrases.english: If the chest wall were pierced opposite it, what would the law be?
It would be a טריפה!
So let the משנה teach 'a pierced chest wall'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fresh challenge to רב נחמן's rule from a different direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that a lung hole sealed by the chest wall is kosher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule were true, a hole in the chest wall would be a separate kind of טריפה. The משנה does not list one, so the rule seems wrong.

steps.title: The same question would apply to a gallbladder sealed by the liver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: by your logic, רבי יוחנן's rule would have the same problem. He says a pierced gallbladder sealed by the liver is kosher, and a hole in the liver over it would make it a טריפה. Yet nobody expects the משנה to list 'a pierced liver.' So the missing chest wall in the משנה proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your logic: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן that a gallbladder that was pierced, with the liver sealing it, is kosher. If the liver were pierced opposite it, what would the law be? A טריפה! So let the משנה teach 'a pierced liver'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב עוקבא by showing that his question would also knock down an accepted rule of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the gallbladder case, a hole in the liver opposite the sealed spot would also make the animal a טריפה. Still, the משנה does not list 'a pierced liver.' So the משנה does not list a case that only matters because it undoes a seal on another organ. The same is true of the chest wall.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own logic

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רב נחמן's rule standing. It also shows that the משנה's list names the organs that become a טריפה when pierced. It does not add a separate entry for every organ whose hole would undo a seal.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that which Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
a gallbladder that was pierced and the liver seals it is kosher,
if the liver were pierced opposite it, what would the law be?
It would be a טריפה!
So let the משנה teach 'a pierced liver'.
phrases.notes: Nobody actually asks this, so the same question about the chest wall falls away too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עוקבא's challenge from Step 21 with a parallel case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case (וליטעמיך): the challenge would also knock down an accepted rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה does not list a pierced chest wall, the chest wall's seal must not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also leaves out a pierced liver, even though it matters in the gallbladder case. So leaving out the chest wall proves nothing, and רב נחמן's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: An organ's seal can save the animal (the chest wall for the lung, the liver for the gallbladder), even though the משנה does not list a hole in the sealing organ as its own טריפה.

steps.title: The משנה only lists organs that cause the טריפה themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The משנה only lists an organ whose own hole makes the animal a טריפה. The chest wall is not such an organ, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה does not list a pierced organ when the animal is not made a טריפה because of it. Here too, since the animal is not made a טריפה because of the chest wall, the משנה does not list it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer from step 22. It explains why neither the liver nor the chest wall appears in the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real cause of the טריפה is the hole in the lung, or in the gallbladder. The chest wall or the liver only matters because it had been sealing that hole. The משנה lists only organs whose own damage is the problem, so a 'pierced chest wall' does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: it (the משנה) does not teach or list it
here too, the same logic applies

steps.whatToRemember: A hole in a sealing organ, like the chest wall or the liver, only matters because it uncovers the original hole. That is why the משנה never lists the sealing organ as its own טריפה.

phrases.english: Rather, when an organ is pierced
and the animal is not made a טריפה because of it
the משנה does not list it;
phrases.notes: In the liver case, the liver is the organ meant here. The real problem is the gallbladder underneath it.

phrases.english: here too, since
the animal is not made a טריפה because of it (the chest wall)
the משנה does not list it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי נִיקְּבָה דְּלָאו מִינֵּיהּ מִיטַּרְפָא – לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 22 by stating the general principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of the משנה's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chest wall decides the animal's status, so the משנה should have listed it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only lists organs whose own hole causes the טריפה. The chest wall only uncovers the lung's hole, so it is left out.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה asks about a lung with cysts
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רבה בר בר חנה asks שמואל about a lung that grew cysts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה asked שמואל: if the lung grew cysts, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a question about a lung that has cysts (צמחין) on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was holes in the lung. Now the question is about growths on the lung's surface. Do they damage the lung enough to make the animal a טריפה?

keyTerms.meaning: growths or cysts, here on the lung

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה מִשְּׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana asked Shmuel:
If the lung grew cysts, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the chest wall discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a lung with cysts a טריפה or כשרה?

steps.title: שמואל rules the animal kosher
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that an animal whose lung has cysts is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a short answer: the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, cysts on the lung do not make the animal a טריפה.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lung with cysts is כשרה.

steps.title: The students doubt it because of רב מתנא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה agrees, but says the students are unsure. רב מתנא ruled that a cyst full of pus is a טריפה and one with clear fluid is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I also say so, but the students are unsure about it. This is because רב מתנא said: if it is full of pus, it is a טריפה; if it has clear fluid, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה raises a difficulty against שמואל's simple ruling. He brings a statement of רב מתנא that seems to say some cysts make the animal a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said all lung cysts are kosher. רב מתנא splits the cases: pus means טריפה, clear fluid means kosher. If רב מתנא was talking about the lung, שמואל's ruling seems too lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן,
phrases.english: He said to him: I also say so,
but the students are unsure about the matter,
since Rav Mattana said:
if it is full of pus, it is a טריפה;
phrases.notes: The 'it' is a cyst. The students assumed he meant a cyst on the lung.

phrases.english: if it has clear fluid, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַתַּלְמִידִים מִזְדַּנְּזִין בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a lung with cysts is כשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב מתנא says a cyst full of pus makes the animal a טריפה. That seems to clash with calling every lung cyst kosher.

steps.title: רב מתנא's rule was about the kidney
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that רב מתנא's rule was said about the kidney, not the lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: that rule was said about the kidney.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל removes the difficulty. רב מתנא was talking about a different organ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pus in a kidney cyst makes the animal a טריפה, but that rule does not carry over to the lung. So שמואל's ruling stands: cysts on the lung are kosher.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rulings. The pus versus clear fluid split is about the kidney. For the lung, שמואל says cysts are כשרה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, cysts on the lung are כשרה. רב מתנא's pus rule applies to the kidney.

phrases.english: He said to him: That rule was said about the kidney.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא בְּכוּלְיָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the other ruling was about a different case (a different organ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מתנא's pus rule was about lung cysts.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב מתנא spoke about the kidney, so lung cysts stay כשרה.

steps.title: A walk through the butchers' market
steps.stepSummary: A story begins. רבי יצחק בר יוסף follows רבי ירמיה in the butchers' market and sees lungs covered with cysts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף was walking after רבי ירמיה in the butchers' market. He saw lungs that were full of cysts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene for a story that will show how a sage actually ruled on lungs with cysts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been ruled yet. The story sets up a real case in the market, which will lead to a practical question.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef was walking
after Rabbi Yirmeya in the butchers' market;
he saw those lungs that were covered with cysts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical story about the cysts discussed in steps 24-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; this sets up a real case of lungs with cysts.

steps.title: A hint asking whether the meat may be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק asks רבי ירמיה if he wants meat, really asking whether this meat is kosher. רבי ירמיה dodges by saying he has no money, and רבי יצחק offers to buy it on credit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Doesn't the master want some meat? He answered: I have no coins. He said: I will buy on credit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק indirectly asks for a ruling by offering to buy the meat. רבי ירמיה tries to avoid answering, but רבי יצחק blocks his excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ירמיה agreed to buy the meat, that would show the meat is kosher. Saying 'I have no money' avoids a ruling, but once credit is offered, he can no longer hide behind it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא בָּעֵי מָר אוּמְצָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master want a piece of meat?
phrases.notes: He is really asking whether meat from these animals is kosher, without asking straight out.

phrases.english: He said to him: I have no money.
He said to him: I will buy it on credit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא בָּעֵי מָר אוּמְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by pressing רבי ירמיה for a ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is meat from animals whose lungs have cysts kosher?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה follows רבי יוחנן's own strictness
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that רבי יוחנן would send such cases to רבי יהודה בר רבי שמעון, who permitted them in the name of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן himself did not agree, so רבי ירמיה will not permit the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: What can I do for you? When people came to רבי יוחנן with this, he sent them to רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון. That sage permitted it in the name of רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון, but רבי יוחנן himself did not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה finally gives his answer. He will not buy the meat, because his teacher רבי יוחנן did not personally permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a lenient opinion, from רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון, that permits lungs with cysts. רבי יוחנן did not forbid people from asking that sage, but he did not hold that way himself. So רבי ירמיה is strict for himself, unlike שמואל's lenient ruling earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not hold that view

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a gap between שמואל, who permits lungs with cysts, and the stricter practice that comes from רבי יוחנן's personal view.

phrases.english: He said to him: What can I do for you?
For when people came before Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁדַּר לְהוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: he would send them before Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמוֹרֵי בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: who ruled on it in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
to permit it,
but he himself (Rabbi Yochanan) did not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אֶעֱבֵיד לָךְ, דְּכִי אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי ירמיה's real answer after his excuse was blocked in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ירמיה does not permit the meat, because רבי יוחנן personally did not accept the lenient view, even though he sent askers to the sage who held it.

steps.title: רבא begins a story about רב נחמן in the market
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts telling what happened when they walked behind רב נחמן in the market.
